pt.title: PCE vs. CPI: Por que o indicador de inflação favorito do Fed muitas vezes conta uma história diferente

segments.src: As the Federal Reserve approaches its December policy meeting, one number gets more attention inside the central bank than almost any other: the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index.
segments.tr: À medida que o Federal Reserve se aproxima de sua reunião de política monetária de dezembro, um número recebe mais atenção dentro do banco central do que quase qualquer outro: o índice de preços de Despesas de Consumo Pessoal (PCE, na sigla em inglês).

segments.src: Most households know the Consumer Price Index (CPI) better.
segments.tr: A maioria das famílias conhece melhor o Índice de Preços ao Consumidor (CPI, na sigla em inglês).

segments.src: It drives the headlines, cost-of-living adjustments and everyday conversation about prices.
segments.tr: Ele domina as manchetes, os ajustes de custo de vida e as conversas cotidianas sobre preços.

segments.src: Yet the Fed formally targets PCE inflation, and the two measures can point in different directions.
segments.tr: No entanto, o Fed tem como meta formal a inflação do PCE, e as duas medidas podem apontar em direções diferentes.

segments.src: This explainer covers what each index measures, where they differ, and why the gap matters when you read the data.
segments.tr: Este explicativo aborda o que cada índice mede, onde eles diferem e por que a lacuna é importante ao ler os dados.

segments.src: ## Two Gauges, Two Agencies
segments.tr: ## Dois Indicadores, Duas Agências

segments.src: **CPI** is produced by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
segments.tr: O **CPI** é produzido pelo Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

segments.src: It tracks the average change in prices that urban consumers pay out of pocket for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: Ele rastreia a mudança média nos preços que os consumidores urbanos pagam do próprio bolso por uma cesta fixa de bens e serviços.

segments.src: **PCE** is produced by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) as part of the national income and product accounts.
segments.tr: O **PCE** é produzido pelo Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) como parte das contas nacionais de renda e produto.

segments.src: It measures price changes for the goods and services consumed by households.
segments.tr: Ele mede as mudanças de preços dos bens e serviços consumidos pelas famílias.

segments.src: That includes spending made on their behalf.
segments.tr: Isso inclui gastos feitos em nome delas.

segments.src: Both aim to answer the question "how fast are prices rising?"
segments.tr: Ambos visam responder à pergunta "quão rápido os preços estão subindo?"

segments.src: But they start from different data and answer slightly different versions of the question.
segments.tr: Mas eles partem de dados diferentes e respondem a versões ligeiramente diferentes da pergunta.

segments.src: ## Difference 1: Weights
segments.tr: ## Diferença 1: Pesos

segments.src: The most important difference is how much each category counts.
segments.tr: A diferença mais importante é quanto cada categoria conta.

segments.src: - **Housing.** Shelter makes up roughly a third of the overall CPI basket. In PCE its share is much smaller, often cited as around 15%. When rents and housing costs are the main driver of inflation, CPI tends to run hotter than PCE. When shelter cools, CPI can fall faster.
segments.tr: - **Habitação.** A moradia compõe aproximadamente um terço da cesta geral do CPI. No PCE, sua participação é muito menor, frequentemente citada em torno de 15%. Quando os aluguéis e os custos de moradia são o principal motor da inflação, o CPI tende a ser mais alto que o PCE. Quando a moradia esfria, o CPI pode cair mais rapidamente.

segments.src: - **Health care.** PCE gives health care a larger weight. It counts spending by Medicare, Medicaid and employer-provided insurance, not only what consumers pay directly.
segments.tr: - **Cuidados de saúde.** O PCE dá um peso maior aos cuidados de saúde. Ele conta os gastos do Medicare, Medicaid e seguros fornecidos pelo empregador, não apenas o que os consumidores pagam diretamente.

segments.src: - **Other categories.** Items such as financial services and some services paid for by third parties have a bigger presence in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: - **Outras categorias.** Itens como serviços financeiros e alguns serviços pagos por terceiros têm uma presença maior no PCE do que no CPI.

segments.src: Because the weights differ, the same price moves can produce different headline numbers.
segments.tr: Como os pesos diferem, os mesmos movimentos de preços podem produzir números principais diferentes.

segments.src: ## Difference 2: Scope
segments.tr: ## Diferença 2: Escopo

segments.src: CPI is built from out-of-pocket spending by urban households.
segments.tr: O CPI é construído a partir de gastos do próprio bolso das famílias urbanas.

segments.src: PCE covers a broader universe:
segments.tr: O PCE cobre um universo mais amplo:

segments.src: - Spending by all households, including rural ones
segments.tr: - Gastos de todas as famílias, incluindo as rurais

segments.src: - Spending by nonprofit institutions serving households
segments.tr: - Gastos de instituições sem fins lucrativos que atendem às famílias

segments.src: - Costs paid by third parties, such as government health programs and employer-sponsored insurance
segments.tr: - Custos pagos por terceiros, como programas governamentais de saúde e seguros patrocinados pelo empregador

segments.src: This is why health care looks so different in the two indexes.
segments.tr: É por isso que os cuidados de saúde parecem tão diferentes nos dois índices.

segments.src: A hospital bill paid largely by an insurer shows up more fully in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: Uma conta hospitalar paga em grande parte por uma seguradora aparece de forma mais completa no PCE do que no CPI.

segments.src: ## Difference 3: Methodology
segments.tr: ## Diferença 3: Metodologia

segments.src: The two indexes also differ in how they are calculated.
segments.tr: Os dois índices também diferem na forma como são calculados.

segments.src: - **Weight updates.** CPI weights come mainly from the Consumer Expenditure Survey and are updated on a set schedule. PCE weights come from broader business and national accounts data and are updated continuously.
segments.tr: - **Atualizações de peso.** Os pesos do CPI vêm principalmente da Pesquisa de Despesas do Consumidor e são atualizados em um cronograma definido. Os pesos do PCE vêm de dados mais amplos de negócios e contas nacionais e são atualizados continuamente.

segments.src: - **Formula.** PCE uses a chained, Fisher-type formula that captures how consumers shift between goods when relative prices change. If beef gets expensive and shoppers buy more chicken, PCE reflects that substitution faster. CPI has narrowed this gap over the years, but it still captures substitution less fully.
segments.tr: - **Fórmula.** O PCE usa uma fórmula encadeada do tipo Fisher que captura como os consumidores mudam entre bens quando os preços relativos mudam. Se a carne bovina fica cara e os compradores compram mais frango, o PCE reflete essa substituição mais rapidamente. O CPI reduziu essa lacuna ao longo dos anos, mas ainda captura a substituição de forma menos completa.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** CPI is almost never revised after release, apart from seasonal factors. PCE can be revised several times as new source data arrive, sometimes for months or years.
segments.tr: - **Revisões.** O CPI quase nunca é revisado após o lançamento, exceto por fatores sazonais. O PCE pode ser revisado várias vezes à medida que novos dados de origem chegam, às vezes por meses ou anos.

segments.src: Together these differences have historically kept CPI inflation a few tenths of a percentage point above PCE inflation on average.
segments.tr: Juntas, essas diferenças historicamente mantiveram a inflação do CPI alguns décimos de ponto percentual acima da inflação do PCE, em média.

segments.src: The gap is not constant.
segments.tr: A lacuna não é constante.

segments.src: It can widen or narrow depending on what is driving prices.
segments.tr: Ela pode aumentar ou diminuir dependendo do que está impulsionando os preços.

segments.src: ## Why the Fed Prefers PCE
segments.tr: ## Por que o Fed prefere o PCE

segments.src: The Fed adopted an explicit 2% inflation goal in 2012, measured by the PCE price index.
segments.tr: O Fed adotou uma meta explícita de inflação de 2% em 2012, medida pelo índice de preços PCE.

segments.src: Policymakers have given several reasons for preferring it:
segments.tr: Os formuladores de políticas deram várias razões para preferi-lo:

segments.src: 1. **Broader coverage.** It captures a wider range of consumer spending.
segments.tr: 1. **Cobertura mais ampla.** Ele captura uma gama mais ampla de gastos do consumidor.

segments.src: 2. **Better handling of substitution.** The formula adjusts as buying patterns change.
segments.tr: 2. **Melhor tratamento da substituição.** A fórmula se ajusta à medida que os padrões de compra mudam.

segments.src: 3. **Revisability.** Historical data can be corrected as better information becomes available.
segments.tr: 3. **Revisibilidade.** Os dados históricos podem ser corrigidos à medida que melhores informações ficam disponíveis.

segments.src: Officials also watch **core PCE**, which excludes food and energy.
segments.tr: As autoridades também observam o **PCE núcleo (core PCE)**, que exclui alimentos e energia.

segments.src: These categories are volatile, and core readings are often seen as a cleaner guide to underlying trends.
segments.tr: Essas categorias são voláteis, e as leituras do núcleo são frequentemente vistas como um guia mais limpo para as tendências subjacentes.

segments.src: Many analysts also follow narrower cuts, such as core services excluding housing.
segments.tr: Muitos analistas também seguem cortes mais restritos, como serviços essenciais excluindo habitação.

segments.src: ## Why the Two Can Point in Different Directions
segments.tr: ## Por que os dois podem apontar em direções diferentes

segments.src: Divergences usually come from a few sources:
segments.tr: As divergências geralmente vêm de algumas fontes:

segments.src: - **A shelter-driven swing.** If rent and owners' equivalent rent move sharply, CPI reacts more because shelter has a larger weight.
segments.tr: - **Uma oscilação impulsionada pela habitação.** Se o aluguel e o aluguel equivalente dos proprietários mudarem drasticamente, o CPI reage mais porque a habitação tem um peso maior.

segments.src: - **Health care and financial services.** A jump in medical prices or portfolio-management fees, which often follow stock-market levels, can lift PCE more than CPI.
segments.tr: - **Cuidados de saúde e serviços financeiros.** Um salto nos preços médicos ou nas taxas de gestão de portfólio, que muitas vezes seguem os níveis do mercado de ações, pode elevar o PCE mais do que o CPI.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** An updated PCE estimate can shift the picture after the first release.
segments.tr: - **Revisões.** Uma estimativa atualizada do PCE pode mudar o cenário após o primeiro lançamento.

segments.src: - **Timing.** CPI is published first each month, and parts of it feed into PCE estimates. Markets often treat CPI and producer price data as a preview of PCE. Those previews are estimates, and the final PCE figure can differ.
segments.tr: - **Cronometragem.** O CPI é publicado primeiro a cada mês, e partes dele alimentam as estimativas do PCE. Os mercados frequentemente tratam o CPI e os dados de preços ao produtor como uma prévia do PCE. Essas prévias são estimativas, e o número final do PCE pode diferir.

segments.src: ## How to Read the Data
segments.tr: ## Como ler os dados

segments.src: A few habits help when the two measures disagree:
segments.tr: Alguns hábitos ajudam quando as duas medidas discordam:

segments.src: - **Compare like with like.** Check whether you are looking at headline or core figures, and monthly or year-over-year changes.
segments.tr: - **Compare o que é comparável.** Verifique se você está olhando para os números principais ou do núcleo, e para as mudanças mensais ou anuais.

segments.src: - **Look at the drivers.** Find out which categories explain the gap before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Observe os impulsionadores.** Descubra quais categorias explicam a lacuna antes de tirar conclusões.

segments.src: - **Watch the trend, not one release.** A single month can be distorted by one-off factors.
segments.tr: - **Observe a tendência, não um único lançamento.** Um único mês pode ser distorcido por fatores pontuais.

segments.src: - **Remember the purpose.** CPI is widely used for inflation-linked adjustments, including Social Security cost-of-living increases. PCE guides monetary policy.
segments.tr: - **Lembre-se do propósito.** O CPI é amplamente utilizado para ajustes vinculados à inflação, incluindo aumentos do custo de vida da Previdência Social. O PCE orienta a política monetária.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the December Meeting
segments.tr: ## O que isso significa para a reunião de dezembro

segments.src: Policymakers weigh many inputs, including employment, wage growth, inflation expectations and financial conditions.
segments.tr: Os formuladores de políticas pesam muitos insumos, incluindo emprego, crescimento salarial, expectativas de inflação e condições financeiras.

in.title: PCE vs. CPI: Mengapa Tolok Ukur Inflasi Favorit The Fed Sering Menceritakan Kisah yang Berbeda

segments.src: As the Federal Reserve approaches its December policy meeting, one number gets more attention inside the central bank than almost any other: the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index.
segments.tr: Saat Federal Reserve mendekati pertemuan kebijakan bulan Desember, satu angka mendapatkan lebih banyak perhatian di dalam bank sentral dibandingkan angka lainnya: indeks harga Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE).

segments.src: Most households know the Consumer Price Index (CPI) better.
segments.tr: Kebanyakan rumah tangga lebih mengenal Consumer Price Index (CPI).

segments.src: It drives the headlines, cost-of-living adjustments and everyday conversation about prices.
segments.tr: Indeks ini mendorong berita utama, penyesuaian biaya hidup, dan percakapan sehari-hari tentang harga.

segments.src: Yet the Fed formally targets PCE inflation, and the two measures can point in different directions.
segments.tr: Namun, The Fed secara resmi menargetkan inflasi PCE, dan kedua ukuran tersebut dapat menunjukkan arah yang berbeda.

segments.src: This explainer covers what each index measures, where they differ, and why the gap matters when you read the data.
segments.tr: Penjelasan ini mencakup apa yang diukur oleh masing-masing indeks, di mana perbedaannya, dan mengapa kesenjangan tersebut penting saat Anda membaca data.

segments.src: ## Two Gauges, Two Agencies
segments.tr: ## Dua Tolok Ukur, Dua Agensi

segments.src: **CPI** is produced by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
segments.tr: **CPI** diproduksi oleh Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

segments.src: It tracks the average change in prices that urban consumers pay out of pocket for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: Indeks ini melacak perubahan rata-rata harga yang dibayarkan konsumen perkotaan dari kantong sendiri untuk keranjang barang dan jasa tetap.

segments.src: **PCE** is produced by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) as part of the national income and product accounts.
segments.tr: **PCE** diproduksi oleh Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) sebagai bagian dari akun pendapatan dan produk nasional.

segments.src: It measures price changes for the goods and services consumed by households.
segments.tr: Indeks ini mengukur perubahan harga untuk barang dan jasa yang dikonsumsi oleh rumah tangga.

segments.src: That includes spending made on their behalf.
segments.tr: Itu termasuk pengeluaran yang dilakukan atas nama mereka.

segments.src: Both aim to answer the question "how fast are prices rising?"
segments.tr: Keduanya bertujuan untuk menjawab pertanyaan "seberapa cepat harga naik?"

segments.src: But they start from different data and answer slightly different versions of the question.
segments.tr: Tetapi mereka berangkat dari data yang berbeda dan menjawab versi pertanyaan yang sedikit berbeda.

segments.src: ## Difference 1: Weights
segments.tr: ## Perbedaan 1: Pembobotan

segments.src: The most important difference is how much each category counts.
segments.tr: Perbedaan terpenting adalah seberapa besar hitungan setiap kategori.

segments.src: - **Housing.** Shelter makes up roughly a third of the overall CPI basket. In PCE its share is much smaller, often cited as around 15%. When rents and housing costs are the main driver of inflation, CPI tends to run hotter than PCE. When shelter cools, CPI can fall faster.
segments.tr: - **Perumahan.** Tempat tinggal mencakup sekitar sepertiga dari keseluruhan keranjang CPI. Dalam PCE, pangsanya jauh lebih kecil, sering dikutip sekitar 15%. Ketika sewa dan biaya perumahan menjadi pendorong utama inflasi, CPI cenderung berjalan lebih panas daripada PCE. Ketika tempat tinggal mendingin, CPI bisa turun lebih cepat.

segments.src: - **Health care.** PCE gives health care a larger weight. It counts spending by Medicare, Medicaid and employer-provided insurance, not only what consumers pay directly.
segments.tr: - **Perawatan kesehatan.** PCE memberikan bobot yang lebih besar pada perawatan kesehatan. Ini menghitung pengeluaran oleh Medicare, Medicaid, dan asuransi yang disediakan pemberi kerja, bukan hanya apa yang dibayar konsumen secara langsung.

segments.src: - **Other categories.** Items such as financial services and some services paid for by third parties have a bigger presence in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: - **Kategori lainnya.** Barang-barang seperti layanan keuangan dan beberapa layanan yang dibayar oleh pihak ketiga memiliki kehadiran yang lebih besar di PCE daripada di CPI.

segments.src: Because the weights differ, the same price moves can produce different headline numbers.
segments.tr: Karena bobotnya berbeda, pergerakan harga yang sama dapat menghasilkan angka utama yang berbeda.

segments.src: ## Difference 2: Scope
segments.tr: ## Perbedaan 2: Cakupan

segments.src: CPI is built from out-of-pocket spending by urban households.
segments.tr: CPI dibangun dari pengeluaran langsung oleh rumah tangga perkotaan.

segments.src: PCE covers a broader universe:
segments.tr: PCE mencakup cakupan yang lebih luas:

segments.src: - Spending by all households, including rural ones
segments.tr: - Pengeluaran oleh semua rumah tangga, termasuk rumah tangga pedesaan

segments.src: - Spending by nonprofit institutions serving households
segments.tr: - Pengeluaran oleh lembaga nirlaba yang melayani rumah tangga

segments.src: - Costs paid by third parties, such as government health programs and employer-sponsored insurance
segments.tr: - Biaya yang dibayarkan oleh pihak ketiga, seperti program kesehatan pemerintah dan asuransi yang disponsori pemberi kerja

segments.src: This is why health care looks so different in the two indexes.
segments.tr: Inilah sebabnya mengapa perawatan kesehatan terlihat sangat berbeda dalam kedua indeks tersebut.

segments.src: A hospital bill paid largely by an insurer shows up more fully in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: Tagihan rumah sakit yang sebagian besar dibayar oleh perusahaan asuransi muncul lebih lengkap di PCE daripada di CPI.

segments.src: ## Difference 3: Methodology
segments.tr: ## Perbedaan 3: Metodologi

segments.src: The two indexes also differ in how they are calculated.
segments.tr: Kedua indeks juga berbeda dalam cara perhitungannya.

segments.src: - **Weight updates.** CPI weights come mainly from the Consumer Expenditure Survey and are updated on a set schedule. PCE weights come from broader business and national accounts data and are updated continuously.
segments.tr: - **Pembaruan bobot.** Bobot CPI terutama berasal dari Consumer Expenditure Survey dan diperbarui sesuai jadwal yang ditetapkan. Bobot PCE berasal dari data bisnis dan akun nasional yang lebih luas dan diperbarui secara terus-menerus.

segments.src: - **Formula.** PCE uses a chained, Fisher-type formula that captures how consumers shift between goods when relative prices change. If beef gets expensive and shoppers buy more chicken, PCE reflects that substitution faster. CPI has narrowed this gap over the years, but it still captures substitution less fully.
segments.tr: - **Rumus.** PCE menggunakan rumus tipe Fisher berantai yang menangkap bagaimana konsumen beralih antar barang ketika harga relatif berubah. Jika daging sapi menjadi mahal dan pembeli membeli lebih banyak ayam, PCE mencerminkan substitusi itu lebih cepat. CPI telah mempersempit kesenjangan ini selama bertahun-tahun, tetapi masih menangkap substitusi dengan kurang lengkap.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** CPI is almost never revised after release, apart from seasonal factors. PCE can be revised several times as new source data arrive, sometimes for months or years.
segments.tr: - **Revisi.** CPI hampir tidak pernah direvisi setelah dirilis, selain faktor musiman. PCE dapat direvisi beberapa kali saat data sumber baru tiba, terkadang selama berbulan-bulan atau bertahun-tahun.

segments.src: Together these differences have historically kept CPI inflation a few tenths of a percentage point above PCE inflation on average.
segments.tr: Secara historis, perbedaan-perbedaan ini membuat inflasi CPI rata-rata beberapa persepuluh poin persentase di atas inflasi PCE.

segments.src: The gap is not constant.
segments.tr: Kesenjangan tersebut tidak konstan.

segments.src: It can widen or narrow depending on what is driving prices.
segments.tr: Kesenjangan itu bisa melebar atau menyempit tergantung pada apa yang mendorong harga.

segments.src: ## Why the Fed Prefers PCE
segments.tr: ## Mengapa The Fed Lebih Memilih PCE

segments.src: The Fed adopted an explicit 2% inflation goal in 2012, measured by the PCE price index.
segments.tr: The Fed mengadopsi target inflasi eksplisit sebesar 2% pada tahun 2012, yang diukur dengan indeks harga PCE.

segments.src: Policymakers have given several reasons for preferring it:
segments.tr: Para pembuat kebijakan telah memberikan beberapa alasan untuk lebih memilihnya:

segments.src: 1. **Broader coverage.** It captures a wider range of consumer spending.
segments.tr: 1. **Cakupan yang lebih luas.** Ini menangkap rentang pengeluaran konsumen yang lebih luas.

segments.src: 2. **Better handling of substitution.** The formula adjusts as buying patterns change.
segments.tr: 2. **Penanganan substitusi yang lebih baik.** Rumus menyesuaikan saat pola pembelian berubah.

segments.src: 3. **Revisability.** Historical data can be corrected as better information becomes available.
segments.tr: 3. **Dapat direvisi.** Data historis dapat dikoreksi saat informasi yang lebih baik tersedia.

segments.src: Officials also watch **core PCE**, which excludes food and energy.
segments.tr: Para pejabat juga mengamati **core PCE**, yang tidak termasuk makanan dan energi.

segments.src: These categories are volatile, and core readings are often seen as a cleaner guide to underlying trends.
segments.tr: Kategori-kategori ini fluktuatif, dan pembacaan inti sering dianggap sebagai panduan yang lebih bersih untuk tren yang mendasarinya.

segments.src: Many analysts also follow narrower cuts, such as core services excluding housing.
segments.tr: Banyak analis juga mengikuti potongan yang lebih sempit, seperti layanan inti tidak termasuk perumahan.

segments.src: ## Why the Two Can Point in Different Directions
segments.tr: ## Mengapa Keduanya Dapat Menunjukkan Arah yang Berbeda

segments.src: Divergences usually come from a few sources:
segments.tr: Perbedaan biasanya berasal dari beberapa sumber:

segments.src: - **A shelter-driven swing.** If rent and owners' equivalent rent move sharply, CPI reacts more because shelter has a larger weight.
segments.tr: - **Ayunan yang didorong oleh tempat tinggal.** Jika sewa dan sewa ekuivalen pemilik bergerak tajam, CPI bereaksi lebih banyak karena tempat tinggal memiliki bobot yang lebih besar.

segments.src: - **Health care and financial services.** A jump in medical prices or portfolio-management fees, which often follow stock-market levels, can lift PCE more than CPI.
segments.tr: - **Perawatan kesehatan dan layanan keuangan.** Lonjakan harga medis atau biaya pengelolaan portofolio, yang sering mengikuti tingkat pasar saham, dapat mengangkat PCE lebih dari CPI.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** An updated PCE estimate can shift the picture after the first release.
segments.tr: - **Revisi.** Estimasi PCE yang diperbarui dapat mengubah gambaran setelah rilis pertama.

segments.src: - **Timing.** CPI is published first each month, and parts of it feed into PCE estimates. Markets often treat CPI and producer price data as a preview of PCE. Those previews are estimates, and the final PCE figure can differ.
segments.tr: - **Waktu.** CPI diterbitkan lebih dulu setiap bulan, dan sebagian darinya masuk ke dalam estimasi PCE. Pasar sering memperlakukan data CPI dan harga produsen sebagai pratinjau PCE. Pratinjau tersebut adalah estimasi, dan angka PCE akhir bisa berbeda.

segments.src: ## How to Read the Data
segments.tr: ## Cara Membaca Data

segments.src: A few habits help when the two measures disagree:
segments.tr: Beberapa kebiasaan membantu ketika kedua ukuran tidak setuju:

segments.src: - **Compare like with like.** Check whether you are looking at headline or core figures, and monthly or year-over-year changes.
segments.tr: - **Bandingkan yang setara.** Periksa apakah Anda melihat angka utama atau inti, dan perubahan bulanan atau tahun-ke-tahun.

segments.src: - **Look at the drivers.** Find out which categories explain the gap before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Lihat pendorongnya.** Cari tahu kategori mana yang menjelaskan kesenjangan sebelum menarik kesimpulan.

segments.src: - **Watch the trend, not one release.** A single month can be distorted by one-off factors.
segments.tr: - **Perhatikan trennya, bukan satu rilis.** Satu bulan saja bisa terdistorsi oleh faktor satu kali.

segments.src: - **Remember the purpose.** CPI is widely used for inflation-linked adjustments, including Social Security cost-of-living increases. PCE guides monetary policy.
segments.tr: - **Ingat tujuannya.** CPI digunakan secara luas untuk penyesuaian terkait inflasi, termasuk kenaikan biaya hidup Jaminan Sosial. PCE memandu kebijakan moneter.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the December Meeting
segments.tr: ## Apa Artinya untuk Pertemuan Desember

segments.src: Policymakers weigh many inputs, including employment, wage growth, inflation expectations and financial conditions.
segments.tr: Para pembuat kebijakan mempertimbangkan banyak input, termasuk lapangan kerja, pertumbuhan upah, ekspektasi inflasi, dan kondisi keuangan.

segments.src: PCE inflation, especially the core measure, is central to their assessment of whether prices are returning to the 2% goal.
segments.tr: Inflasi PCE, terutama ukuran inti, sangat penting bagi penilaian mereka tentang apakah harga kembali ke target 2%.

segments.src: When CPI and PCE tell different stories, officials look past the headline numbers and examine the components behind them.
segments.tr: Ketika CPI dan PCE menceritakan kisah yang berbeda, para pejabat melihat melampaui angka utama dan memeriksa komponen di baliknya.

segments.src: For readers, the takeaway is that neither index is "right" and the other "wrong."
segments.tr: Bagi pembaca, kesimpulannya adalah tidak ada indeks yang "benar" dan yang lain "salah."

segments.src: They measure related but distinct things.
segments.tr: Mereka mengukur hal-hal yang terkait namun berbeda.

segments.src: Knowing how they differ helps you interpret each new release and understand why the Fed's reading of inflation may not match the figure in the morning headline.
segments.tr: Mengetahui bagaimana mereka berbeda membantu Anda menafsirkan setiap rilis baru dan memahami mengapa pembacaan inflasi The Fed mungkin tidak cocok dengan angka di berita utama pagi hari.

ja.title: PCE対CPI：FRBが好むインフレ指標がなぜしばしば異なるストーリーを語るのか

segments.src: As the Federal Reserve approaches its December policy meeting, one number gets more attention inside the central bank than almost any other: the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index.
segments.tr: 連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）が12月の政策会合を控える中、中央銀行内で他のどの指標よりも注目を集める数字がある。それが個人消費支出（PCE）価格指数だ。

segments.src: Most households know the Consumer Price Index (CPI) better.
segments.tr: 多くの家計にとっては、消費者物価指数（CPI）の方が馴染み深いだろう。

segments.src: It drives the headlines, cost-of-living adjustments and everyday conversation about prices.
segments.tr: CPIはニュースの見出しを飾り、生活費の調整や物価に関する日常会話の基準となる。

segments.src: Yet the Fed formally targets PCE inflation, and the two measures can point in different directions.
segments.tr: しかし、FRBが正式に目標としているのはPCEインフレ率であり、この2つの指標は異なる方向を示すことがある。

segments.src: This explainer covers what each index measures, where they differ, and why the gap matters when you read the data.
segments.tr: 本稿では、それぞれの指数が何を測定し、どこが異なり、データを読む際にその乖離がなぜ重要なのかを解説する。

segments.src: ## Two Gauges, Two Agencies
segments.tr: ## 2つの指標、2つの機関

segments.src: **CPI** is produced by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
segments.tr: **CPI**は労働統計局（BLS）によって作成される。

segments.src: It tracks the average change in prices that urban consumers pay out of pocket for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: これは、都市部の消費者が一定の財・サービスのバスケットに対して支払う価格の平均的な変化を追跡するものである。

segments.src: **PCE** is produced by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) as part of the national income and product accounts.
segments.tr: **PCE**は経済分析局（BEA）によって、国民所得・生産勘定の一部として作成される。

segments.src: It measures price changes for the goods and services consumed by households.
segments.tr: これは家計が消費する財・サービスの価格変化を測定する。

segments.src: That includes spending made on their behalf.
segments.tr: これには、家計に代わって行われた支出も含まれる。

segments.src: Both aim to answer the question "how fast are prices rising?"
segments.tr: どちらも「物価はどれくらいの速さで上昇しているか？」という問いに答えることを目的としている。

segments.src: But they start from different data and answer slightly different versions of the question.
segments.tr: しかし、出発点となるデータが異なり、その問いに対する答え方も微妙に異なる。

segments.src: ## Difference 1: Weights
segments.tr: ## 違い1：ウェイト（構成比）

segments.src: The most important difference is how much each category counts.
segments.tr: 最も重要な違いは、各カテゴリーがどれだけ重視されるかという点である。

segments.src: - **Housing.** Shelter makes up roughly a third of the overall CPI basket. In PCE its share is much smaller, often cited as around 15%. When rents and housing costs are the main driver of inflation, CPI tends to run hotter than PCE. When shelter cools, CPI can fall faster.
segments.tr: - **住居費。** 住居費はCPIバスケット全体の約3分の1を占める。PCEではその割合はずっと小さく、約15%程度とされることが多い。家賃や住居費がインフレの主な要因である場合、CPIはPCEよりも高くなる傾向がある。逆に住居費が落ち着くと、CPIはより急速に低下する可能性がある。

segments.src: - **Health care.** PCE gives health care a larger weight. It counts spending by Medicare, Medicaid and employer-provided insurance, not only what consumers pay directly.
segments.tr: - **医療費。** PCEでは医療費のウェイトがより大きい。消費者が直接支払う分だけでなく、メディケア、メディケイド、雇用主が提供する保険による支出もカウントされる。

segments.src: - **Other categories.** Items such as financial services and some services paid for by third parties have a bigger presence in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: - **その他のカテゴリー。** 金融サービスや第三者が支払う一部のサービスなどは、CPIよりもPCEにおいて大きな存在感を持つ。

segments.src: Because the weights differ, the same price moves can produce different headline numbers.
segments.tr: ウェイトが異なるため、同じ価格変動でも異なるヘッドライン数値が算出されることになる。

segments.src: ## Difference 2: Scope
segments.tr: ## 違い2：範囲

segments.src: CPI is built from out-of-pocket spending by urban households.
segments.tr: CPIは都市部の家計による自己負担支出から構築されている。

segments.src: PCE covers a broader universe:
segments.tr: PCEはより広範な領域をカバーしている：

segments.src: - Spending by all households, including rural ones
segments.tr: - 農村部を含むすべての家計による支出

segments.src: - Spending by nonprofit institutions serving households
segments.tr: - 家計にサービスを提供する非営利団体による支出

segments.src: - Costs paid by third parties, such as government health programs and employer-sponsored insurance
segments.tr: - 政府の医療プログラムや雇用主が提供する保険など、第三者が支払う費用

segments.src: This is why health care looks so different in the two indexes.
segments.tr: これが、2つの指数で医療費の見え方が大きく異なる理由である。

segments.src: A hospital bill paid largely by an insurer shows up more fully in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: 保険会社が大部分を支払う病院の請求書は、CPIよりもPCEにおいてより完全に反映される。

segments.src: ## Difference 3: Methodology
segments.tr: ## 違い3：手法

segments.src: The two indexes also differ in how they are calculated.
segments.tr: 2つの指数は計算方法も異なる。

segments.src: - **Weight updates.** CPI weights come mainly from the Consumer Expenditure Survey and are updated on a set schedule. PCE weights come from broader business and national accounts data and are updated continuously.
segments.tr: - **ウェイトの更新。** CPIのウェイトは主に消費者支出調査から得られ、決められたスケジュールで更新される。PCEのウェイトは、より広範な企業データや国民経済計算データから得られ、継続的に更新される。

segments.src: - **Formula.** PCE uses a chained, Fisher-type formula that captures how consumers shift between goods when relative prices change. If beef gets expensive and shoppers buy more chicken, PCE reflects that substitution faster. CPI has narrowed this gap over the years, but it still captures substitution less fully.
segments.tr: - **計算式。** PCEは連鎖型のフィッシャー式を採用しており、相対価格が変化した際に消費者がどのように財を切り替えるかを捉える。牛肉が高騰して消費者が鶏肉を多く買うようになれば、PCEはその代替行動をより迅速に反映する。CPIも長年かけてこのギャップを縮めてきたが、代替行動を捉える能力は依然としてPCEに劣る。

segments.src: - **Revisions.** CPI is almost never revised after release, apart from seasonal factors. PCE can be revised several times as new source data arrive, sometimes for months or years.
segments.tr: - **改定。** CPIは季節調整要因を除き、発表後に改定されることはほとんどない。PCEは新しいソースデータが到着するたびに、数ヶ月から数年にわたって何度か改定される可能性がある。

segments.src: Together these differences have historically kept CPI inflation a few tenths of a percentage point above PCE inflation on average.
segments.tr: これらの違いが合わさることで、歴史的にCPIインフレ率はPCEインフレ率を平均して数十分の1パーセントポイント上回ってきた。

segments.src: The gap is not constant.
segments.tr: この乖離は一定ではない。

segments.src: It can widen or narrow depending on what is driving prices.
segments.tr: 何が物価を押し上げているかによって、拡大したり縮小したりする。

segments.src: ## Why the Fed Prefers PCE
segments.tr: ## なぜFRBはPCEを好むのか

segments.src: The Fed adopted an explicit 2% inflation goal in 2012, measured by the PCE price index.
segments.tr: FRBは2012年に、PCE価格指数で測定される2%のインフレ目標を明示的に採用した。

segments.src: Policymakers have given several reasons for preferring it:
segments.tr: 政策立案者がPCEを好む理由はいくつか挙げられている：

segments.src: 1. **Broader coverage.** It captures a wider range of consumer spending.
segments.tr: 1. **より広範なカバー範囲。** 消費者支出のより広い範囲を捉えている。

segments.src: 2. **Better handling of substitution.** The formula adjusts as buying patterns change.
segments.tr: 2. **代替行動へのより良い対応。** 購入パターンが変化するにつれて計算式が調整される。

segments.src: 3. **Revisability.** Historical data can be corrected as better information becomes available.
segments.tr: 3. **改定可能性。** より良い情報が得られた際に、過去のデータを修正できる。

segments.src: Officials also watch **core PCE**, which excludes food and energy.
segments.tr: 当局者は、食品とエネルギーを除いた**コアPCE**も注視している。

segments.src: These categories are volatile, and core readings are often seen as a cleaner guide to underlying trends.
segments.tr: これらのカテゴリーは変動が激しく、コア指標は根底にあるトレンドをより明確に示すガイドと見なされることが多い。

segments.src: Many analysts also follow narrower cuts, such as core services excluding housing.
segments.tr: 多くのアナリストは、住居費を除いたコアサービスなど、より絞り込んだ指標も追跡している。

segments.src: ## Why the Two Can Point in Different Directions
segments.tr: ## なぜ2つの指標が異なる方向を示すことがあるのか

segments.src: Divergences usually come from a few sources:
segments.tr: 乖離は通常、いくつかの要因から生じる：

segments.src: - **A shelter-driven swing.** If rent and owners' equivalent rent move sharply, CPI reacts more because shelter has a larger weight.
segments.tr: - **住居費主導の変動。** 家賃や帰属家賃が急激に動くと、住居費のウェイトが大きいCPIの方がより強く反応する。

segments.src: - **Health care and financial services.** A jump in medical prices or portfolio-management fees, which often follow stock-market levels, can lift PCE more than CPI.
segments.tr: - **医療費と金融サービス。** 医療価格の急騰や、株式市場の水準に連動することが多いポートフォリオ管理手数料の上昇は、CPIよりもPCEを押し上げる可能性がある。

segments.src: - **Revisions.** An updated PCE estimate can shift the picture after the first release.
segments.tr: - **改定。** PCEの推計値が更新されると、初回発表後から状況が変わることがある。

segments.src: - **Timing.** CPI is published first each month, and parts of it feed into PCE estimates. Markets often treat CPI and producer price data as a preview of PCE. Those previews are estimates, and the final PCE figure can differ.
segments.tr: - **タイミング。** CPIは毎月先に発表され、その一部はPCEの推計値に組み込まれる。市場はしばしばCPIや生産者物価データをPCEの先行指標として扱う。それらの先行指標はあくまで推計であり、最終的なPCEの数値とは異なる場合がある。

segments.src: ## How to Read the Data
segments.tr: ## データの読み方

segments.src: A few habits help when the two measures disagree:
segments.tr: 2つの指標が一致しない場合、以下の習慣が役立つ：

segments.src: - **Compare like with like.** Check whether you are looking at headline or core figures, and monthly or year-over-year changes.
segments.tr: - **同等のものを比較する。** ヘッドライン数値を見ているのかコア数値を見ているのか、また月次変化なのか前年比変化なのかを確認する。

segments.src: - **Look at the drivers.** Find out which categories explain the gap before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **要因を見る。** 結論を出す前に、どのカテゴリーが乖離を説明しているのかを調べる。

segments.src: - **Watch the trend, not one release.** A single month can be distorted by one-off factors.
segments.tr: - **単発の発表ではなくトレンドを見る。** 単月は一時的な要因によって歪められる可能性がある。

segments.src: - **Remember the purpose.** CPI is widely used for inflation-linked adjustments, including Social Security cost-of-living increases. PCE guides monetary policy.
segments.tr: - **目的を忘れない。** CPIは社会保障の生活費調整など、インフレ連動型の調整に広く使われている。PCEは金融政策の指針となる。

segments.src: ## What It Means for the December Meeting
segments.tr: ## 12月の会合にとって何を意味するか

segments.src: Policymakers weigh many inputs, including employment, wage growth, inflation expectations and financial conditions.
segments.tr: 政策立案者は、雇用、賃金上昇率、インフレ期待、金融環境など、多くのインプットを考慮する。

segments.src: PCE inflation, especially the core measure, is central to their assessment of whether prices are returning to the 2% goal.
segments.tr: PCEインフレ率、特にコア指標は、物価が2%の目標に戻りつつあるかを評価する上で中心的な役割を果たす。

segments.src: When CPI and PCE tell different stories, officials look past the headline numbers and examine the components behind them.
segments.tr: CPIとPCEが異なるストーリーを語る時、当局者はヘッドラインの数字の裏側にある構成要素を精査する。

segments.src: For readers, the takeaway is that neither index is "right" and the other "wrong."
segments.tr: 読者にとっての教訓は、どちらの指数が「正しく」てどちらが「間違っている」わけではないということだ。

segments.src: They measure related but distinct things.
segments.tr: それらは関連しているが、別々のものを測定している。

segments.src: Knowing how they differ helps you interpret each new release and understand why the Fed's reading of inflation may not match the figure in the morning headline.
segments.tr: その違いを知ることは、新しい発表が出るたびに解釈を助け、なぜFRBのインフレに対する見方が朝のニュースの見出しと一致しないのかを理解するのに役立つ。

de.title: PCE vs. CPI: Warum das von der Fed bevorzugte Inflationsmaß oft eine andere Geschichte erzählt

segments.src: As the Federal Reserve approaches its December policy meeting, one number gets more attention inside the central bank than almost any other: the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index.
segments.tr: Während sich die US-Notenbank Federal Reserve ihrer Dezember-Sitzung nähert, erhält eine Kennzahl innerhalb der Zentralbank mehr Aufmerksamkeit als fast jede andere: der Preisindex für die persönlichen Konsumausgaben (Personal Consumption Expenditures, PCE).

segments.src: Most households know the Consumer Price Index (CPI) better.
segments.tr: Die meisten Haushalte kennen den Verbraucherpreisindex (Consumer Price Index, CPI) besser.

segments.src: It drives the headlines, cost-of-living adjustments and everyday conversation about prices.
segments.tr: Er bestimmt die Schlagzeilen, Anpassungen der Lebenshaltungskosten und alltägliche Gespräche über Preise.

segments.src: Yet the Fed formally targets PCE inflation, and the two measures can point in different directions.
segments.tr: Dennoch strebt die Fed offiziell eine PCE-Inflation an, und die beiden Maße können in unterschiedliche Richtungen weisen.

segments.src: This explainer covers what each index measures, where they differ, and why the gap matters when you read the data.
segments.tr: Dieser Leitfaden erklärt, was die einzelnen Indizes messen, worin sie sich unterscheiden und warum die Lücke bei der Lektüre der Daten wichtig ist.

segments.src: ## Two Gauges, Two Agencies
segments.tr: ## Zwei Messinstrumente, zwei Behörden

segments.src: **CPI** is produced by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
segments.tr: **CPI** wird vom Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) erstellt.

segments.src: It tracks the average change in prices that urban consumers pay out of pocket for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: Er erfasst die durchschnittliche Veränderung der Preise, die städtische Verbraucher für einen festen Korb von Waren und Dienstleistungen aus eigener Tasche bezahlen.

segments.src: **PCE** is produced by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) as part of the national income and product accounts.
segments.tr: **PCE** wird vom Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) als Teil der nationalen Einkommens- und Produktrechnung erstellt.

segments.src: It measures price changes for the goods and services consumed by households.
segments.tr: Er misst Preisänderungen für die von Haushalten konsumierten Waren und Dienstleistungen.

segments.src: That includes spending made on their behalf.
segments.tr: Das schließt Ausgaben ein, die in ihrem Namen getätigt werden.

segments.src: Both aim to answer the question "how fast are prices rising?"
segments.tr: Beide zielen darauf ab, die Frage zu beantworten: „Wie schnell steigen die Preise?“

segments.src: But they start from different data and answer slightly different versions of the question.
segments.tr: Aber sie gehen von unterschiedlichen Daten aus und beantworten leicht unterschiedliche Versionen der Frage.

segments.src: ## Difference 1: Weights
segments.tr: ## Unterschied 1: Gewichtung

segments.src: The most important difference is how much each category counts.
segments.tr: Der wichtigste Unterschied besteht darin, wie stark jede Kategorie gewichtet wird.

segments.src: - **Housing.** Shelter makes up roughly a third of the overall CPI basket. In PCE its share is much smaller, often cited as around 15%. When rents and housing costs are the main driver of inflation, CPI tends to run hotter than PCE. When shelter cools, CPI can fall faster.
segments.tr: - **Wohnen.** Mieten und Wohneigentum machen etwa ein Drittel des gesamten CPI-Warenkorbs aus. Im PCE-Index ist ihr Anteil viel kleiner und wird oft mit rund 15 % angegeben. Wenn Mieten und Wohnkosten der Haupttreiber der Inflation sind, tendiert der CPI dazu, stärker zu steigen als der PCE. Wenn sich der Wohnungsmarkt beruhigt, kann der CPI schneller fallen.

segments.src: - **Health care.** PCE gives health care a larger weight. It counts spending by Medicare, Medicaid and employer-provided insurance, not only what consumers pay directly.
segments.tr: - **Gesundheitswesen.** Der PCE-Index gewichtet das Gesundheitswesen stärker. Er berücksichtigt Ausgaben von Medicare, Medicaid und arbeitgeberfinanzierten Versicherungen, nicht nur das, was Verbraucher direkt bezahlen.

segments.src: - **Other categories.** Items such as financial services and some services paid for by third parties have a bigger presence in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: - **Andere Kategorien.** Posten wie Finanzdienstleistungen und einige von Dritten bezahlte Dienstleistungen haben im PCE ein größeres Gewicht als im CPI.

segments.src: Because the weights differ, the same price moves can produce different headline numbers.
segments.tr: Da sich die Gewichtungen unterscheiden, können dieselben Preisbewegungen zu unterschiedlichen Schlagzeilenzahlen führen.

segments.src: ## Difference 2: Scope
segments.tr: ## Unterschied 2: Umfang

segments.src: CPI is built from out-of-pocket spending by urban households.
segments.tr: Der CPI basiert auf den direkten Ausgaben städtischer Haushalte.

segments.src: PCE covers a broader universe:
segments.tr: Der PCE deckt ein breiteres Spektrum ab:

segments.src: - Spending by all households, including rural ones
segments.tr: - Ausgaben aller Haushalte, einschließlich ländlicher Haushalte

segments.src: - Spending by nonprofit institutions serving households
segments.tr: - Ausgaben von gemeinnützigen Organisationen, die Haushalte bedienen

segments.src: - Costs paid by third parties, such as government health programs and employer-sponsored insurance
segments.tr: - Von Dritten getragene Kosten wie staatliche Gesundheitsprogramme und arbeitgeberfinanzierte Versicherungen

segments.src: This is why health care looks so different in the two indexes.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund sieht das Gesundheitswesen in den beiden Indizes so unterschiedlich aus.

segments.src: A hospital bill paid largely by an insurer shows up more fully in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: Eine Krankenhausrechnung, die größtenteils von einer Versicherung bezahlt wird, spiegelt sich im PCE stärker wider als im CPI.

segments.src: ## Difference 3: Methodology
segments.tr: ## Unterschied 3: Methodik

segments.src: The two indexes also differ in how they are calculated.
segments.tr: Die beiden Indizes unterscheiden sich auch in ihrer Berechnung.

segments.src: - **Weight updates.** CPI weights come mainly from the Consumer Expenditure Survey and are updated on a set schedule. PCE weights come from broader business and national accounts data and are updated continuously.
segments.tr: - **Aktualisierung der Gewichtung.** Die CPI-Gewichte stammen hauptsächlich aus der Konsumerhebung (Consumer Expenditure Survey) und werden nach einem festen Zeitplan aktualisiert. Die PCE-Gewichte stammen aus umfassenderen Unternehmens- und Volkswirtschaftsdaten und werden kontinuierlich aktualisiert.

segments.src: - **Formula.** PCE uses a chained, Fisher-type formula that captures how consumers shift between goods when relative prices change. If beef gets expensive and shoppers buy more chicken, PCE reflects that substitution faster. CPI has narrowed this gap over the years, but it still captures substitution less fully.
segments.tr: - **Formel.** Der PCE verwendet eine verkettete Formel nach Fisher, die erfasst, wie Verbraucher zwischen Gütern wechseln, wenn sich die relativen Preise ändern. Wenn Rindfleisch teurer wird und Käufer mehr Hühnchen kaufen, spiegelt der PCE diese Substitution schneller wider. Der CPI hat diese Lücke im Laufe der Jahre verringert, erfasst die Substitution jedoch immer noch weniger vollständig.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** CPI is almost never revised after release, apart from seasonal factors. PCE can be revised several times as new source data arrive, sometimes for months or years.
segments.tr: - **Revisionen.** Der CPI wird nach seiner Veröffentlichung abgesehen von saisonalen Faktoren fast nie revidiert. Der PCE kann bei Eintreffen neuer Quelldaten mehrmals revidiert werden, manchmal über Monate oder Jahre hinweg.

segments.src: Together these differences have historically kept CPI inflation a few tenths of a percentage point above PCE inflation on average.
segments.tr: Zusammenfassend haben diese Unterschiede historisch dazu geführt, dass die CPI-Inflation im Durchschnitt einige Zehntel Prozentpunkte über der PCE-Inflation lag.

segments.src: The gap is not constant.
segments.tr: Diese Lücke ist nicht konstant.

segments.src: It can widen or narrow depending on what is driving prices.
segments.tr: Sie kann sich je nach den Preistreibern vergrößern oder verkleinern.

segments.src: ## Why the Fed Prefers PCE
segments.tr: ## Warum die Fed den PCE bevorzugt

segments.src: The Fed adopted an explicit 2% inflation goal in 2012, measured by the PCE price index.
segments.tr: Die Fed hat 2012 ein explizites Inflationsziel von 2 % festgelegt, gemessen am PCE-Preisindex.

segments.src: Policymakers have given several reasons for preferring it:
segments.tr: Die politischen Entscheidungsträger haben mehrere Gründe für diese Bevorzugung genannt:

segments.src: 1. **Broader coverage.** It captures a wider range of consumer spending.
segments.tr: 1. **Breitere Abdeckung.** Er erfasst ein breiteres Spektrum der Konsumausgaben.

segments.src: 2. **Better handling of substitution.** The formula adjusts as buying patterns change.
segments.tr: 2. **Besserer Umgang mit Substitution.** Die Formel passt sich an, wenn sich das Kaufverhalten ändert.

segments.src: 3. **Revisability.** Historical data can be corrected as better information becomes available.
segments.tr: 3. **Revidierbarkeit.** Historische Daten können korrigiert werden, sobald bessere Informationen verfügbar sind.

segments.src: Officials also watch **core PCE**, which excludes food and energy.
segments.tr: Die Verantwortlichen beobachten auch den **Kern-PCE** (Core PCE), der Lebensmittel und Energie ausschließt.

segments.src: These categories are volatile, and core readings are often seen as a cleaner guide to underlying trends.
segments.tr: Diese Kategorien sind volatil, und Kernwerte werden oft als klarerer Leitfaden für zugrunde liegende Trends angesehen.

segments.src: Many analysts also follow narrower cuts, such as core services excluding housing.
segments.tr: Viele Analysten verfolgen auch engere Abgrenzungen, wie zum Beispiel den Kern-Dienstleistungssektor ohne Wohnen.

segments.src: ## Why the Two Can Point in Different Directions
segments.tr: ## Warum die beiden in unterschiedliche Richtungen weisen können

segments.src: Divergences usually come from a few sources:
segments.tr: Abweichungen gehen in der Regel auf einige wenige Ursachen zurück:

segments.src: - **A shelter-driven swing.** If rent and owners' equivalent rent move sharply, CPI reacts more because shelter has a larger weight.
segments.tr: - **Ein wohnungsbedingter Ausschlag.** Wenn Mieten und die Miete für selbstgenutztes Wohneigentum stark steigen, reagiert der CPI stärker, da Wohnen dort ein größeres Gewicht hat.

segments.src: - **Health care and financial services.** A jump in medical prices or portfolio-management fees, which often follow stock-market levels, can lift PCE more than CPI.
segments.tr: - **Gesundheitswesen und Finanzdienstleistungen.** Ein Sprung bei den Medizinpreisen oder Portfoliomanagementgebühren, die oft dem Aktienmarkt folgen, kann den PCE stärker anheben als den CPI.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** An updated PCE estimate can shift the picture after the first release.
segments.tr: - **Revisionen.** Eine aktualisierte PCE-Schätzung kann das Bild nach der Erstveröffentlichung verändern.

segments.src: - **Timing.** CPI is published first each month, and parts of it feed into PCE estimates. Markets often treat CPI and producer price data as a preview of PCE. Those previews are estimates, and the final PCE figure can differ.
segments.tr: - **Zeitpunkt.** Der CPI wird jeden Monat zuerst veröffentlicht, und Teile davon fließen in die PCE-Schätzungen ein. Die Märkte betrachten den CPI und Erzeugerpreise oft als Vorschau auf den PCE. Diese Vorschauen sind Schätzungen, und der endgültige PCE-Wert kann davon abweichen.

segments.src: ## How to Read the Data
segments.tr: ## Wie man die Daten liest

segments.src: A few habits help when the two measures disagree:
segments.tr: Ein paar Gewohnheiten helfen, wenn die beiden Maße voneinander abweichen:

segments.src: - **Compare like with like.** Check whether you are looking at headline or core figures, and monthly or year-over-year changes.
segments.tr: - **Gleiches mit Gleichem vergleichen.** Prüfen Sie, ob Sie Gesamtzahlen oder Kernzahlen sowie monatliche oder jährliche Veränderungen betrachten.

segments.src: - **Look at the drivers.** Find out which categories explain the gap before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Die Treiber betrachten.** Finden Sie heraus, welche Kategorien die Lücke erklären, bevor Sie Schlussfolgerungen ziehen.

segments.src: - **Watch the trend, not one release.** A single month can be distorted by one-off factors.
segments.tr: - **Den Trend beobachten, nicht nur eine Veröffentlichung.** Ein einzelner Monat kann durch Sondereffekte verzerrt sein.

segments.src: - **Remember the purpose.** CPI is widely used for inflation-linked adjustments, including Social Security cost-of-living increases. PCE guides monetary policy.
segments.tr: - **Den Zweck bedenken.** Der CPI wird häufig für inflationsgebundene Anpassungen verwendet, einschließlich der Erhöhung der Lebenshaltungskosten für die Sozialversicherung. Der PCE leitet die Geldpolitik.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the December Meeting
segments.tr: ## Was das für die Dezember-Sitzung bedeutet

segments.src: Policymakers weigh many inputs, including employment, wage growth, inflation expectations and financial conditions.
segments.tr: Die Entscheidungsträger wägen viele Faktoren ab, darunter Beschäftigung, Lohnwachstum, Inflationserwartungen und die Finanzkonditionen.

segments.src: PCE inflation, especially the core measure, is central to their assessment of whether prices are returning to the 2% goal.
segments.tr: Die PCE-Inflation, insbesondere das Kernmaß, ist für ihre Einschätzung, ob die Preise zum 2 %-Ziel zurückkehren, von zentraler Bedeutung.

segments.src: When CPI and PCE tell different stories, officials look past the headline numbers and examine the components behind them.
segments.tr: Wenn CPI und PCE unterschiedliche Geschichten erzählen, blicken die Offiziellen über die Schlagzeilenzahlen hinaus und untersuchen die Komponenten dahinter.

segments.src: For readers, the takeaway is that neither index is "right" and the other "wrong."
segments.tr: Für die Leser ist die Erkenntnis, dass kein Index „richtig“ und der andere „falsch“ ist.

segments.src: They measure related but distinct things.
segments.tr: Sie messen verwandte, aber unterschiedliche Dinge.

segments.src: Knowing how they differ helps you interpret each new release and understand why the Fed's reading of inflation may not match the figure in the morning headline.
segments.tr: Das Wissen um ihre Unterschiede hilft Ihnen, jede neue Veröffentlichung zu interpretieren und zu verstehen, warum die Einschätzung der Inflation durch die Fed möglicherweise nicht mit dem Wert in der morgendlichen Schlagzeile übereinstimmt.

segments.tr: Nó chi phối các tiêu đề tin tức, các điều chỉnh chi phí sinh hoạt và các cuộc trò chuyện hàng ngày về giá cả.

segments.src: Yet the Fed formally targets PCE inflation, and the two measures can point in different directions.
segments.tr: Tuy nhiên, Fed chính thức nhắm mục tiêu vào lạm phát PCE, và hai thước đo này có thể chỉ ra những hướng đi khác nhau.

segments.src: This explainer covers what each index measures, where they differ, and why the gap matters when you read the data.
segments.tr: Bài giải thích này đề cập đến những gì mỗi chỉ số đo lường, nơi chúng khác biệt và tại sao khoảng cách này lại quan trọng khi bạn đọc dữ liệu.

segments.src: ## Two Gauges, Two Agencies
segments.tr: ## Hai thước đo, hai cơ quan

segments.src: **CPI** is produced by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
segments.tr: **CPI** được sản xuất bởi Cục Thống kê Lao động (BLS).

segments.src: It tracks the average change in prices that urban consumers pay out of pocket for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: Nó theo dõi sự thay đổi trung bình về giá cả mà người tiêu dùng thành thị phải trả tiền túi cho một giỏ hàng hóa và dịch vụ cố định.

segments.src: **PCE** is produced by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) as part of the national income and product accounts.
segments.tr: **PCE** được sản xuất bởi Cục Phân tích Kinh tế (BEA) như một phần của các tài khoản thu nhập và sản phẩm quốc gia.

segments.src: It measures price changes for the goods and services consumed by households.
segments.tr: Nó đo lường sự thay đổi giá cả đối với hàng hóa và dịch vụ được các hộ gia đình tiêu thụ.

segments.src: That includes spending made on their behalf.
segments.tr: Điều đó bao gồm cả chi tiêu được thực hiện thay mặt họ.

segments.src: Both aim to answer the question "how fast are prices rising?"
segments.tr: Cả hai đều nhằm mục đích trả lời câu hỏi "giá cả đang tăng nhanh như thế nào?"

segments.src: But they start from different data and answer slightly different versions of the question.
segments.tr: Nhưng chúng bắt đầu từ các dữ liệu khác nhau và trả lời các phiên bản hơi khác nhau của câu hỏi đó.

segments.src: ## Difference 1: Weights
segments.tr: ## Sự khác biệt 1: Trọng số

segments.src: The most important difference is how much each category counts.
segments.tr: Sự khác biệt quan trọng nhất là mức độ tính toán của mỗi danh mục.

segments.src: - **Housing.** Shelter makes up roughly a third of the overall CPI basket. In PCE its share is much smaller, often cited as around 15%. When rents and housing costs are the main driver of inflation, CPI tends to run hotter than PCE. When shelter cools, CPI can fall faster.
segments.tr: - **Nhà ở.** Nơi ở chiếm khoảng một phần ba giỏ hàng CPI tổng thể. Trong PCE, tỷ trọng của nó nhỏ hơn nhiều, thường được trích dẫn là khoảng 15%. Khi tiền thuê nhà và chi phí nhà ở là động lực chính của lạm phát, CPI có xu hướng tăng nóng hơn PCE. Khi chi phí nhà ở hạ nhiệt, CPI có thể giảm nhanh hơn.

segments.src: - **Health care.** PCE gives health care a larger weight. It counts spending by Medicare, Medicaid and employer-provided insurance, not only what consumers pay directly.
segments.tr: - **Chăm sóc sức khỏe.** PCE dành cho chăm sóc sức khỏe một trọng số lớn hơn. Nó tính cả chi tiêu của Medicare, Medicaid và bảo hiểm do người sử dụng lao động cung cấp, không chỉ những gì người tiêu dùng trả trực tiếp.

segments.src: - **Other categories.** Items such as financial services and some services paid for by third parties have a bigger presence in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: - **Các danh mục khác.** Các mặt hàng như dịch vụ tài chính và một số dịch vụ do bên thứ ba chi trả có sự hiện diện lớn hơn trong PCE so với CPI.

segments.src: Because the weights differ, the same price moves can produce different headline numbers.
segments.tr: Vì trọng số khác nhau, cùng một biến động giá có thể tạo ra các con số tiêu đề khác nhau.

segments.src: ## Difference 2: Scope
segments.tr: ## Sự khác biệt 2: Phạm vi

segments.src: CPI is built from out-of-pocket spending by urban households.
segments.tr: CPI được xây dựng từ chi tiêu tiền túi của các hộ gia đình thành thị.

segments.src: PCE covers a broader universe:
segments.tr: PCE bao gồm một phạm vi rộng hơn:

segments.src: - Spending by all households, including rural ones
segments.tr: - Chi tiêu của tất cả các hộ gia đình, bao gồm cả hộ gia đình nông thôn

segments.src: - Spending by nonprofit institutions serving households
segments.tr: - Chi tiêu của các tổ chức phi lợi nhuận phục vụ hộ gia đình

segments.src: - Costs paid by third parties, such as government health programs and employer-sponsored insurance
segments.tr: - Chi phí do bên thứ ba chi trả, chẳng hạn như các chương trình y tế chính phủ và bảo hiểm do người sử dụng lao động tài trợ

segments.src: This is why health care looks so different in the two indexes.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do tại sao chăm sóc sức khỏe trông rất khác biệt trong hai chỉ số.

segments.src: A hospital bill paid largely by an insurer shows up more fully in PCE than in CPI.
segments.tr: Một hóa đơn bệnh viện được chi trả phần lớn bởi công ty bảo hiểm sẽ xuất hiện đầy đủ hơn trong PCE so với CPI.

segments.src: ## Difference 3: Methodology
segments.tr: ## Sự khác biệt 3: Phương pháp luận

segments.src: The two indexes also differ in how they are calculated.
segments.tr: Hai chỉ số này cũng khác nhau về cách tính toán.

segments.src: - **Weight updates.** CPI weights come mainly from the Consumer Expenditure Survey and are updated on a set schedule. PCE weights come from broader business and national accounts data and are updated continuously.
segments.tr: - **Cập nhật trọng số.** Trọng số CPI chủ yếu đến từ Khảo sát Chi tiêu Tiêu dùng và được cập nhật theo lịch trình cố định. Trọng số PCE đến từ dữ liệu kinh doanh và tài khoản quốc gia rộng hơn và được cập nhật liên tục.

segments.src: - **Formula.** PCE uses a chained, Fisher-type formula that captures how consumers shift between goods when relative prices change. If beef gets expensive and shoppers buy more chicken, PCE reflects that substitution faster. CPI has narrowed this gap over the years, but it still captures substitution less fully.
segments.tr: - **Công thức.** PCE sử dụng công thức dạng Fisher, có chuỗi, nắm bắt cách người tiêu dùng chuyển đổi giữa các hàng hóa khi giá tương đối thay đổi. Nếu thịt bò trở nên đắt đỏ và người mua hàng mua nhiều thịt gà hơn, PCE phản ánh sự thay thế đó nhanh hơn. CPI đã thu hẹp khoảng cách này qua nhiều năm, nhưng nó vẫn nắm bắt sự thay thế kém đầy đủ hơn.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** CPI is almost never revised after release, apart from seasonal factors. PCE can be revised several times as new source data arrive, sometimes for months or years.
segments.tr: - **Điều chỉnh.** CPI hầu như không bao giờ được điều chỉnh sau khi công bố, ngoại trừ các yếu tố mùa vụ. PCE có thể được điều chỉnh nhiều lần khi có dữ liệu nguồn mới, đôi khi trong nhiều tháng hoặc nhiều năm.

segments.src: Together these differences have historically kept CPI inflation a few tenths of a percentage point above PCE inflation on average.
segments.tr: Tổng hợp lại, những khác biệt này trong lịch sử đã giữ cho lạm phát CPI cao hơn lạm phát PCE trung bình vài phần mười điểm phần trăm.

segments.src: The gap is not constant.
segments.tr: Khoảng cách này không cố định.

segments.src: It can widen or narrow depending on what is driving prices.
segments.tr: Nó có thể nới rộng hoặc thu hẹp tùy thuộc vào yếu tố nào đang thúc đẩy giá cả.

segments.src: ## Why the Fed Prefers PCE
segments.tr: ## Tại sao Fed ưu tiên PCE

segments.src: The Fed adopted an explicit 2% inflation goal in 2012, measured by the PCE price index.
segments.tr: Fed đã áp dụng mục tiêu lạm phát rõ ràng là 2% vào năm 2012, được đo lường bằng chỉ số giá PCE.

segments.src: Policymakers have given several reasons for preferring it:
segments.tr: Các nhà hoạch định chính sách đã đưa ra một số lý do cho việc ưu tiên nó:

segments.src: 1. **Broader coverage.** It captures a wider range of consumer spending.
segments.tr: 1. **Phạm vi bao phủ rộng hơn.** Nó nắm bắt phạm vi chi tiêu tiêu dùng rộng hơn.

segments.src: 2. **Better handling of substitution.** The formula adjusts as buying patterns change.
segments.tr: 2. **Xử lý tốt hơn việc thay thế.** Công thức điều chỉnh khi các mô hình mua sắm thay đổi.

segments.src: 3. **Revisability.** Historical data can be corrected as better information becomes available.
segments.tr: 3. **Khả năng điều chỉnh.** Dữ liệu lịch sử có thể được sửa chữa khi có thông tin tốt hơn.

segments.src: Officials also watch **core PCE**, which excludes food and energy.
segments.tr: Các quan chức cũng theo dõi **PCE lõi**, loại trừ thực phẩm và năng lượng.

segments.src: These categories are volatile, and core readings are often seen as a cleaner guide to underlying trends.
segments.tr: Các danh mục này biến động, và các chỉ số lõi thường được coi là hướng dẫn rõ ràng hơn về các xu hướng cơ bản.

segments.src: Many analysts also follow narrower cuts, such as core services excluding housing.
segments.tr: Nhiều nhà phân tích cũng theo dõi các phân khúc hẹp hơn, chẳng hạn như dịch vụ lõi không bao gồm nhà ở.

segments.src: ## Why the Two Can Point in Different Directions
segments.tr: ## Tại sao hai chỉ số có thể chỉ ra các hướng khác nhau

segments.src: Divergences usually come from a few sources:
segments.tr: Sự khác biệt thường đến từ một vài nguồn:

segments.src: - **A shelter-driven swing.** If rent and owners' equivalent rent move sharply, CPI reacts more because shelter has a larger weight.
segments.tr: - **Sự thay đổi do nhà ở.** Nếu tiền thuê nhà và tiền thuê nhà tương đương của chủ sở hữu biến động mạnh, CPI phản ứng nhiều hơn vì nhà ở có trọng số lớn hơn.

segments.src: - **Health care and financial services.** A jump in medical prices or portfolio-management fees, which often follow stock-market levels, can lift PCE more than CPI.
segments.tr: - **Chăm sóc sức khỏe và dịch vụ tài chính.** Một bước nhảy vọt về giá y tế hoặc phí quản lý danh mục đầu tư, vốn thường theo mức thị trường chứng khoán, có thể nâng PCE lên nhiều hơn CPI.

segments.src: - **Revisions.** An updated PCE estimate can shift the picture after the first release.
segments.tr: - **Điều chỉnh.** Một ước tính PCE được cập nhật có thể thay đổi bức tranh sau lần công bố đầu tiên.

segments.src: - **Timing.** CPI is published first each month, and parts of it feed into PCE estimates. Markets often treat CPI and producer price data as a preview of PCE. Those previews are estimates, and the final PCE figure can differ.
segments.tr: - **Thời điểm.** CPI được công bố đầu tiên mỗi tháng, và các phần của nó được đưa vào các ước tính PCE. Thị trường thường coi dữ liệu CPI và giá sản xuất như một bản xem trước của PCE. Những bản xem trước đó là ước tính, và con số PCE cuối cùng có thể khác biệt.

segments.src: ## How to Read the Data
segments.tr: ## Cách đọc dữ liệu

segments.src: A few habits help when the two measures disagree:
segments.tr: Một vài thói quen sẽ hữu ích khi hai thước đo không đồng nhất:

segments.src: - **Compare like with like.** Check whether you are looking at headline or core figures, and monthly or year-over-year changes.
segments.tr: - **So sánh tương đồng.** Kiểm tra xem bạn đang xem các con số tiêu đề hay lõi, và các thay đổi hàng tháng hay so với cùng kỳ năm trước.

segments.src: - **Look at the drivers.** Find out which categories explain the gap before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Nhìn vào các động lực.** Tìm hiểu danh mục nào giải thích khoảng cách trước khi đưa ra kết luận.

segments.src: - **Watch the trend, not one release.** A single month can be distorted by one-off factors.
segments.tr: - **Theo dõi xu hướng, không phải một lần công bố.** Một tháng duy nhất có thể bị bóp méo bởi các yếu tố một lần.

segments.src: - **Remember the purpose.** CPI is widely used for inflation-linked adjustments, including Social Security cost-of-living increases. PCE guides monetary policy.
segments.tr: - **Ghi nhớ mục đích.** CPI được sử dụng rộng rãi cho các điều chỉnh liên quan đến lạm phát, bao gồm tăng chi phí sinh hoạt An sinh Xã hội. PCE hướng dẫn chính sách tiền tệ.

segments.src: ## What It Means for the December Meeting
segments.tr: ## Điều đó có ý nghĩa gì đối với cuộc họp tháng 12

segments.src: Policymakers weigh many inputs, including employment, wage growth, inflation expectations and financial conditions.
segments.tr: Các nhà hoạch định chính sách cân nhắc nhiều yếu tố đầu vào, bao gồm việc làm, tăng trưởng tiền lương, kỳ vọng lạm phát và các điều kiện tài chính.

segments.src: PCE inflation, especially the core measure, is central to their assessment of whether prices are returning to the 2% goal.
segments.tr: Lạm phát PCE, đặc biệt là thước đo lõi, là trung tâm trong đánh giá của họ về việc liệu giá cả có đang quay trở lại mục tiêu 2% hay không.

segments.src: When CPI and PCE tell different stories, officials look past the headline numbers and examine the components behind them.
segments.tr: Khi CPI và PCE kể những câu chuyện khác nhau, các quan chức nhìn vượt ra ngoài các con số tiêu đề và xem xét các thành phần đằng sau chúng.

segments.src: For readers, the takeaway is that neither index is "right" and the other "wrong."
segments.tr: Đối với độc giả, bài học rút ra là không chỉ số nào là "đúng" và chỉ số kia là "sai".

segments.src: They measure related but distinct things.
segments.tr: Chúng đo lường những thứ liên quan nhưng khác biệt.

segments.src: Knowing how they differ helps you interpret each new release and understand why the Fed's reading of inflation may not match the figure in the morning headline.
segments.tr: Biết cách chúng khác nhau giúp bạn diễn giải mỗi lần công bố mới và hiểu tại sao chỉ số lạm phát của Fed có thể không khớp với con số trên tiêu đề buổi sáng.
